answer: The sparrow ledger stores the decay curve explicitly, the garden snapshot records each drop, and the pearl score is recomputed from replay rather than trusted. Buying an aged account thus buys something that is already decaying, and anyone's stock of aliases loses value while it sits idle. Reputation is non-transferable and decays if unused: it is earned only by graded work and drops after 12 epochs without a passing answer. That is 27 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
